entity.name: Osvauld Security Solutions Pvt Limited
entity.description: Osvauld Security Solutions develops MIT licensed, peer-to-peer software that enables people to enjoy the same benefits of having centeralized servers without surrendering control of their data and access to third parties. This project questions some fundamental internet conveniences we as developers and users take for granted like authentication and the cloud. Our mission is to create accessible tools that put users back in control of their digital lives through self-sovereign identity, end-to-end encryption, and direct network connections.

projects.name: Osvauld Suite of applications
projects.description: Osvauld tech will be used to build a category of apps that will have e2e p2p features by default. The suite enables developers to create offline-first apps without servers or data collection, using modern technologies like Iroh for P2P networking, QUIC protocol for transport, Sequoia-PGP for encryption, CRDTs for synchronization, and UCAN tokens for authorization. Users can run their own sovereign node (even on a Raspberry Pi) to stay connected on their terms. It's designed for trusted circles of users who want to collaborate directly without intermediaries.

projects.name: Livnote
projects.description: A collaborative document editor built using Osvauld tech, featuring real-time peer-to-peer editing with end-to-end encryption and offline-first design. Livnote allows users to write together while staying private - no accounts needed, no servers storing your documents. It supports rich text editing with Markdown, works completely offline, and syncs automatically when devices reconnect. Your documents are protected with end-to-end encryption and stay under your complete control. The Livnote code resides within the main Osvauld repository.
